stages.name: Active Directory and Veeam Credential Harvesting

scenario.summary: Threat actors utilized Bing SEO poisoning to deliver Bumblebee malware via trojanized software installers, leading to the deployment of AdaptixC2 for network discovery. The attackers leveraged RDP over SSH tunnels to move laterally and harvest credentials from NTDS.dit and LSASS before exfiltrating 75GB of data and deploying Akira ransomware.

meta.rationale: Focus the hunt on file servers, domain controllers, and backup infrastructure (e.g., Veeam servers), as these were specifically targeted for bulk data theft and encryption in this scenario.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary is exfiltrating bulk data via SFTP using FileZilla and executing Akira ransomware, evidenced by massive outbound network transfers and the destruction of Volume Shadow Copies.

hunt.name: Akira Ransomware Exfiltration and Impact
hunt.description: This hunt identifies the final, high-impact phase of an Akira ransomware intrusion. It scopes for the execution of known exfiltration tools and the ransomware binary itself (locker.exe), then corroborates this with behavioral evidence: bulk network transfers to rare destinations—matching the 75GB volume reported—and the deletion of system recovery options via shadow copy removal. An agent triages these signals to confirm if a host has reached the final stage of encryption, enabling immediate containment before widespread business disruption occurs.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_original_file_name, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{exfil_tools}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_original_file_name) || ',') > 0 OR instr(',' || '{{ransomware_binaries}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_original_file_name) || ',') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Locate execution of the reported exfiltration tools or ransomware binaries by matching original file names to bypass renaming evasion.
config.expected_signal: A hit names the host and binary (e.g., locker.exe renamed or FileZilla). Silence suggests these specific binaries did not run in the lookback window.

primitive_config.label: Identify Suspect Processes
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_original_file_name, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{exfil_tools}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_original_file_name) || ',') > 0 OR instr(',' || '{{ransomware_binaries}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_original_file_name) || ',') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: A hit names the host and binary (e.g., locker.exe renamed or FileZilla). Silence suggests these specific binaries did not run in the lookback window.

config.content: SELECT dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, SUM(traffic_bytes) AS total_bytes, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_network_connection WHERE state_kind = 'log' AND traffic_bytes > 104857600 AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port HAVING host_count < 3 ORDER BY total_bytes DESC
config.description: Identify hosts pushing massive outbound volume (over 100MB) to destinations seen on very few hosts, characteristic of data theft.
config.expected_signal: One or two hosts pushing huge volume to a unique IP, especially on port 22 (SFTP). Benign noise includes backup servers; outliers represent potential exfiltration.

primitive_config.label: Bulk Exfiltration Stacking
primitive_config.content: SELECT dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, SUM(traffic_bytes) AS total_bytes, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_network_connection WHERE state_kind = 'log' AND traffic_bytes > 104857600 AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port HAVING host_count < 3 ORDER BY total_bytes DESC
primitive_config.expected: One or two hosts pushing huge volume to a unique IP, especially on port 22 (SFTP). Benign noise includes backup servers; outliers represent potential exfiltration.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{impact_admin_tools}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_name) || ',') > 0 OR instr(',' || '{{impact_admin_tools}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_original_file_name) || ',') > 0) AND LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%shadow%' AND LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%delete%' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Detect the final precursor to ransomware impact: the deletion of Volume Shadow Copies using administrative tools.
config.expected_signal: Process rows showing tools like vssadmin or wmic used to delete shadows. This is a high-confidence indicator of ransomware preparation.
